title: CPA FAR Score Release Dates: Late 2026 to Mid-2027
description: The AICPA's target FAR score release dates from November 2026 to July 2027, how the data file cutoff works, and the quarterly schedule that starts in July 2027.
intro: FAR (Financial Accounting and Reporting) is a Core section of the CPA Exam, so you can schedule it at any time of the year. Your score, though, comes out on set dates. If you have a job start, a state deadline, or the next section in mind, the release date can matter as much as the test date. This page lists the AICPA's published target dates for FAR from November 2026 through July 2027, explains how to read the table, and covers the bigger change planned for July 2027. All dates come from the AICPA schedule as checked on October 30, 2026, and the AICPA says every date is a target that can change.

sections.heading: The table works by cutoff date, not test date
sections.body:
The AICPA table for the Core sections (AUD, FAR and REG) has two columns. The first is the date by which **the AICPA receives your exam data file**. The second is your **target score release date**.

That first column is easy to misread. It is not the day you sit for FAR. Prometric, the company that runs the test centers, sends your exam file to the AICPA, and the AICPA notes that your exam cannot be scored until it has that file. So the row that applies to you depends on when the file arrives, not on when you finished the exam.

The practical meaning: if you test right before a cutoff, the file may arrive after it, and your score would follow the next row in the table. The AICPA does not say how long the transfer takes, so do not plan on testing on the cutoff day itself.

sections.heading: Remaining 2026 cycle: four rows left
sections.body:
These are the AICPA's 2026 Core rows that are still ahead as of October 30, 2026. The counts in brackets are days from October 30, 2026, the date this page was published.

- File received by **November 15** (16 days) → target release **November 24** (25 days)
- File received by **December 8** (39 days) → target release **December 16** (47 days)
- File received by **December 31** (62 days) → target release **January 12, 2027** (74 days)

One more row, file received by October 23 with a target release of November 10, has already closed for receipt. If you tested in October and the file reached the AICPA by October 23, November 10 is your target date. If it arrived later, look at the November 24 row.

Notice how the gaps differ. A file that arrives by November 15 has a target release only 9 days later. A file that arrives by December 31 waits 12 days, until January 12, because the release crosses into the new year.

sections.heading: January to July 2027: the last rolling rows
sections.body:
The 2027 Core table uses the same two columns. Here is the full list for the first half of 2027:

1. File by January 23 → release February 9
2. File by February 14 → release February 23
3. File by March 9 → release March 17
4. File by March 31 → release April 9
5. File by April 23 → release May 11
6. File by May 16 → release May 25
7. File by June 8 → release June 16
8. File by June 30 → release July 13

That is eight release dates in about six months. If you want a quick result, some rows are shorter than others. For example, a file received by February 14 has a target release 9 days later, while a file received by April 23 waits until May 11.

sections.heading: From July 2027: one release date per quarter
sections.body:
The AICPA says the CPA Exam moves to a new technology delivery platform beginning in July 2027, with changes to the user interface. It has published an adjusted schedule for the year after that change, and it looks very different for FAR.

Instead of a rolling table, each quarter has a testing period and one target release date:

- Test **July 12 to September 30, 2027** → release **October 19, 2027**
- Test **October 1 to December 15, 2027** → release **December 28, 2027**
- Test **January 1 to March 15, 2028** → release **March 28, 2028**
- Test **April 1 to June 15, 2028** → release **June 27, 2028**

Two things stand out. First, a FAR exam taken early in a period, such as mid-July 2027, has a target release in mid-October, about three months later. Second, the listed Core testing periods leave a gap: the 2027 rolling table ends with files received by June 30, and the next period starts July 12. After the first period, each one ends on the 15th of the quarter's last month (December 15, March 15, June 15).

If a fast FAR result matters to you, the rolling rows before July 2027 give you more release dates to choose from. The AICPA marks all of these dates as subject to change, so check the schedule again before you book.

sections.heading: Why the date matters for your other sections
sections.body:
You have to pass all four sections (three Core sections and one Discipline section) within a credit window. The AICPA describes that window as at least 30 months, and as long as three years in some states. Your state board of accountancy sets the exact rule, including when the clock starts, so check it directly.

The release date also tells you when you will know what to study next. FAR has the lowest pass rate of the three Core sections in the AICPA's 2026 figures: 43.46% in Q1, 42.47% in Q2, and 44.49% in Q3, or 43.54% for the year so far. If you do not pass a section, you also receive a Candidate Performance Report that assesses your performance on that section. Knowing the release date ahead of time lets you decide whether to start the next section while you wait or keep FAR material fresh in case you need it again.

sections.heading: Plan your FAR date in three steps
sections.body:
1. **Pick the release date you want** from the lists above. Choose it by what it lets you do: start a job, meet a state deadline, or schedule the next section.
2. **Look at the cutoff on that row and book well before it.** The cutoff is when the AICPA must have your file, not your test day. Leave yourself room for the file transfer.
3. **Check the AICPA page again before you book and before test day.** These are target dates, and the AICPA says they can change.

While you wait for your score, short practice sets help you keep the material fresh. On this site, the FAR practice covers the multiple-choice part only, grouped by the three blueprint areas: Financial Reporting (30–40%), Select Balance Sheet Accounts (30–40%), and Select Transactions (25–35%).

faq.question: Is the CPA Exam graded on a curve, so my result depends on who tested the same month?
faq.answer: No. The AICPA says scores are not curved and there is no pass-fail quota. The release schedule only controls when you see your score, not how it is calculated. You need a 75 on the 0–99 scale to pass.

faq.question: Do BAR, ISC and TCP follow the same release dates as FAR?
faq.answer: No. Discipline sections are given only in the first month of each quarter. For example, the AICPA lists October 1–31, 2026 testing with a December 15, 2026 target release, then January 1–31, 2027 with March 16, and April 1–30, 2027 with June 9.

faq.question: What if my score is not out on the target date?
faq.answer: The AICPA calls these target dates and says they can change. Also, your exam cannot be scored until the AICPA receives your file from Prometric, so a file that arrives after a cutoff falls under a later row. Check the official schedule for the current dates.
